MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. One unit costs Ksh 250. What is the cost of 4 bottles of cooking oil? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,010
   B. Ksh 1,000
   C. Ksh 254
   D. Ksh 750

2. How can you make Ksh 50 using only 10 shilling coins? (1 mark)
   A. Fifty coins
   B. Five coins
   C. Two coins
   D. Ten coins

3. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 650, Ksh 800 and Ksh 1,900. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 3,250
   B. Ksh 3,360
   C. Ksh 3,450
   D. Ksh 3,350

4. Why do people prepare a shopping list? (1 mark)
   A. To remember everything and not spend more than they have
   B. To avoid using money
   C. To make shops close early
   D. To buy as many things as possible

5. Which way do the hands of a clock move? (1 mark)
   A. Sideways
   B. Anticlockwise
   C. Up and down
   D. Clockwise

6. A bottle top is usually tightened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. sideways
   B. clockwise
   C. anticlockwise
   D. up and down

7. Kip faces East and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. East
   C. North
   D. South

8. What does the size of an angle depend on? (1 mark)
   A. The number of arms
   B. The colour of the arms
   C. How far apart the arms are
   D. How long the arms are

9. A quarter turn makes (1 mark)
   A. no angle
   B. a right angle
   C. a straight line
   D. a full turn

10. How many right angles make a straight line? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 1
   C. 4
   D. 3

11. What is the next shape in the pattern square, triangle, square, triangle, square, ...? (1 mark)
   A. Square
   B. Circle
   C. Triangle
   D. Rectangle

12. How many straight sides does a rectangle have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 5
   D. 2

13. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with no equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 3
   C. 1
   D. 2

14. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are walking or car together? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 6
   C. 9
   D. 8

15. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. How many are NOT green? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 12
   C. 8
   D. 9

16. In a tally chart, 2 groups of five and 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 14
   B. 15
   C. 13
   D. 19

17. What is data? (1 mark)
   A. Information that we collect
   B. A kind of shape
   C. A unit of time
   D. A measuring tape

18. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many more are there of mango than of banana? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 1
   C. 7
   D. 2

19. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are mango or pawpaw together? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 6
   C. 5
   D. 4

20. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. lorry
   B. boda boda
   C. matatu
   D. bus

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A bicycle costs Ksh 6,500, a helmet Ksh 1,750 and a lock Ksh 850. Find the total cost. (3 marks)

22. Change Ksh 12 to cents and 1,250 cents to shillings. (2 marks)

23. Explain how to prepare a shopping list of three items and find its total cost. (4 marks)

24. Find and name three objects in the classroom that show a rectangle, a circle and a triangle. (3 marks)

25. Describe the difference between a clockwise and an anticlockwise turn. (2 marks)

26. Name two things at home or school that are turned clockwise to tighten or close them. (2 marks)

27. Explain what a right angle is. State how many right angles there are in (a) a rectangle, (b) a straight line, (c) a full turn. (5 marks)

28. Show two different ways to make Ksh 50 using coins and notes. (2 marks)

29. A school uniform costs a shirt Ksh 650, shorts Ksh 800 and shoes Ksh 1,900. Find the total cost and the change from Ksh 5,000. (4 marks)

30. Explain why a table is better than raw data for answering questions. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Ksh 1,000
   Cost = number × price = 4 × 250 = Ksh 1,000.

2. B — Five coins
   5 × 10 = 50, so five 10 shilling coins make Ksh 50.

3. D — Ksh 3,350
   Add the three costs: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350.

4. A — To remember everything and not spend more than they have
   A list helps us remember what we need and plan our spending.

5. D — Clockwise
   The hands of a clock move in the direction we call clockwise.

6. B — clockwise
   Tightening a bottle top means turning it clockwise.

7. C — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives North.

8. C — How far apart the arms are
   The size depends on the opening between the arms, not on their length.

9. B — a right angle
   A quarter turn sweeps out a right angle.

10. A — 2
   A straight line is a half turn, which is two right angles.

11. C — Triangle
   The pattern alternates between a square and a triangle, so a triangle comes next.

12. A — 4
   A rectangle has four straight sides.

13. A — 0
   No fold makes the two halves match.

14. A — 7
   6 + 1 = 7.

15. C — 8
   10 − 2 = 8.

16. A — 14
   2 × 5 + 4 = 14.

17. A — Information that we collect
   Data is information such as counts or names that we collect to answer questions.

18. B — 1
   4 − 3 = 1.

19. C — 5
   4 + 1 = 5.

20. C — matatu
   The biggest number is 5, which belongs to matatu.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 9,100
   Working / marking points: 6,500 + 1,750 = 8,250 (1 mark); 8,250 + 850 (1 mark); Ksh 9,100 (1 mark).

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 12 = 1,200 cents; 1,250 cents = Ksh 12.50
   Working / marking points: 12 × 100 = 1,200 (1 mark); 1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so Ksh 12.50 (1 mark).

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what is needed, write the three items with numbers, find the price of each, work out the cost of each item, and add the costs to get the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for choosing items, 1 mark for writing quantity, 1 mark for prices, 1 mark for adding the costs.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example a blackboard (rectangle), a clock face (circle) and a set square (triangle).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object matched to a shape.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clockwise turn goes the same way as the hands of a clock. An anticlockwise turn goes the opposite way.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example a bottle top or a screw, and a tap being closed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: A right angle is a square corner, made by a quarter turn. (a) 4 (b) 2 (c) 4
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for explaining a right angle (square corner or quarter turn), 1 mark for each of (a) 4, (b) 2 and (c) 4.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: one Ksh 50 note; or five Ksh 10 coins; or two Ksh 20 coins and one Ksh 10 coin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 3,350; change Ksh 1,650
   Working / marking points: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350 (2 marks); 5,000 − 3,350 = 1,650 (2 marks).

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table puts the data in order under headings, is neat and easy to read, and shows totals. Raw data is untidy and easy to misread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point up to 3.
